# Experiments: Message Campaigns

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported channels
> 
>   * Push (Web, Android, iOS)
>   * Email
> 


Campaign experiments allow you to compare different creative variants to find what's most effective for your audience. For example, you can add multiple variants with different call-to-action buttons or titles to see which one drives more conversions.

* * *

## 

Limitations

  * Recurring schedules are not supported.
  * Once an experiment campaign starts running, it can no longer be edited.
  * Once an experiment campaign is stopped, it can't be restarted.



* * *

## 

Create an experiment

Experiments can be added when creating an [email](doc:campaigns-message-create-email) or [push](doc:campaigns-message-create-push) message campaign. You can distribute variants to your campaign audience in two ways:

  * Static distribution: Manually set an audience distribution.
  * Winner distribution: Conduct a test to see which variant performs the best. Set the sample audience size for each variant and configure test parameters, and after the test is completed, the best-performing variant will be used for the campaign.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> An experiment campaign can't be edited once it has started running, so remember to verify your configuration before publishing the campaign.

### 

Static distribution

Manually set a percentage of the campaign audience who should receive each variant.

![](https://files.readme.io/ad0ca21f88f68af07ffcf7e3093b087a05ad1d569aa633bda5425fcce1deca54-experiments-push-static-distribution.png)

### 

Winner distribution

Find the best-performing variant by setting the sample audience size for each variant and configuring the test parameters.

  1. **Distribution method** , select **Winner distribution**.
  2. For each variant, enter the percentage of the audience you want to use for sampling.
  3. Under **Winning metric** select the performance metric to measure.
     1. For each metric, you can choose to use **Total** or **Unique** event counts:
        1. **Total** : Each event is counted once.
        2. **Unique** : If a user completes the same event multiple times, the event is only counted once. The number of unique events is an approximation with a <1% margin of error.
  4. Under **Test duration** , configure how long you'd like the test to continue before a winning variant is selected.
  5. Add a creative for each variant.
  6. Click **Next** after you finish setting up the experiment.



In the following example, three variants are randomly and equally distributed for a total 10% of users for sampling. After 30 minutes, the variant with the best performance becomes the winning variant.

![](https://files.readme.io/f8ca24d5f332ff5759820c4e7c30218f259d388be8d9e818e21d6fa756a161a0-experiments-push-winner-distribution.png)

# Getting Started with Campaigns

Easily create automated, personalized campaigns for every channel.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you begin
> 
> Before creating a campaign, ensure you've:
> 
>   * Worked with your developers to [integrate the Appier SDK](doc:sdk-getting-started) and [collect data](doc:user-data-collection).
>   * Created an [audience segment](doc:segments-create).
> 


Automating marketing campaigns allows you to precisely customize your goal, target audience, and core message to deliver personalized experiences to the right audience at the perfect moment. Get started by understanding the basic campaign components, then learn how to launch your first campaign.

* * *

## 

Campaign components

While different campaign types support different settings and features, for example, different channel types or creatives, the following building blocks are shared by all campaigns types.

Component| Description  
---|---  
Audience| Who to send the campaign to. For example:  
• Users who made a purchase in the last 7 days  
• Users who created an account in the past 60 days  
• Email subscribers with items in their shopping cart  
  
Channel| Where the campaign will be sent. Set up your channels before creating campaigns.  
Sending conditions| How the campaign will be sent. Campaigns can be sent in different ways, for example:• Manually from the AIQUA dashboard.  
• On preset a schedule every Monday at 10:00 AM.  
• Triggered by a `page_viewed` event in the checkout page.  
  
Creative| What to send in the campaign. Examples of creatives include:  
• A carousel of images showcasing a variety of new products.  
• An in-web campaign promoting a seasonal sale with a discount code.  
  
* * *

## 

Launch your first campaign

### 

1\. Set up your marketing channels

Set up the marketing channels you'd like to use to send campaigns.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> In-app and in-web campaigns
> 
> You can start delivering in-app and in-web campaigns [integrating your mobile app or website with the Appier SDK](doc:sdk-getting-started).

# Email

Set up and launch email campaigns.

You can integrate AIQUA with an email service provider to send targeted email campaigns to your users. Use AIQUA's audience segmentation and [dynamic content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives) features to better personalize and optimize your messages.

To ensure successful delivery and subscriber management, complete the following setup steps before you create your first email campaign:

  1. Connect your email service provider
  2. Manage user subscriptions
  3. Launch and measure your campaigns



* * *

## 

1\. Connect your email service provider

Contact your Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#e4819797bb979194948b9690a48594948d8196ca878b89)) to integrate your account with an email service provider before sending emails.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Some third-party providers don't support performance tracking metrics, such as impressions, clicks, or conversions. AIQUA can't display these metrics for those providers.

* * *

## 

2\. Manage user subscriptions

Get user consent before sending campaigns and configure clear unsubscribe options to stay compliant with email regulations. Ensure that each campaign includes a clear unsubscribe option, and keep your subscription lists up to date. To learn more, see [Managing user subscriptions](doc:campaigns-getting-started-email-manage-subscriptions).

* * *

## 

3\. Launch and measure your campaigns

After you complete your email setup, you can create and monitor your campaigns in AIQUA.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you launch
> 
>   * Test your campaign: Add your email to the [test segment](doc:segments-test-segment#email-campaigns) and use the **Send test creative** button to preview your campaign.
>   * Set up IP warmup: Start with small send volumes and gradually increase over several weeks to improve deliverability. For a recommended schedule, see [IP Warmup](doc:campaigns-getting-started-email-ip-warmup).
>

# Managing Email Subscriptions

Manage user subscriptions to stay compliant with email regulations and maintain user experience.

## 

Subscribe users to email campaigns

AIQUA automatically subscribes email addresses when you add them through:

  * The Appier SDK attribute logging methods
  * [Bulk upload offline Users API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users)
  * [Update user profiles](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes)



AIQUA converts all email addresses to lowercase and deduplicates them across segments, reports, and the unsubscription list. For example, `[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)` and `[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)` are treated as the same address.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Obtain users consent
> 
> Always obtain explicit user consent before adding email addresses to AIQUA and sending email campaigns. Provide a clear unsubscribe option in every email.

* * *

## 

Update email subscription status

Configure how users can unsubscribe from your campaigns:

  * Email list-unsubscribe header: Set up a one-click unsubscribe link in the email header through your **Account settings** :
    * [**Use Appier 's default unsubscribe URL**](doc:user-settings#use-appiers-default-unsubscribe-url): AIQUA automatically updates the unsubscribed email list when users click the link.
    * [**Use a custom URL**](doc:user-settings#use-a-custom-url): Handle unsubscribes in your own system. AIQUA sends a `POST` request to your URL when users click the unsubscribe link.
  * Unsubscribe links in the editor: Add unsubscribe links to your email using the [**Drag and drop editor**](doc:creatives-email-drag-and-drop-editor). AIQUA automatically updates subscription status automatically when users click these links.
  * Use the AIQUA API to update subscription status when users change their email preferences:
    * [Add emails to the unsubscribed list](ref:add-emails-to-unsubscribed-email-list).
    * [Remove emails from the unsubscribed list](ref:remove-emails-from-unsubscribed-email-list).



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Users in the [Test Segment](doc:segments-test-segment#email-campaigns) receive test emails even when they're unsubscribed, allowing you to test email content before sending to your audience.

### 

How AIQUA handles unsubscribed users

When users unsubscribe through any method above, AIQUA automatically:

  * Sets the `email_unsubscribe` user attribute to `true`.
  * Removes their email addresses from the **Email subscribers** count in the [segment list](doc:segments-segment-list#user-and-subscriber-count).
  * Adds their email addresses to the internal unsubscribed list.



This prevents unsubscribed users from receiving future email campaigns.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> Always use the methods above to manage subscriptions. Don't manually change the `email_unsubscribe` attribute using SDK methods, user profile updates, or the Bulk Upload API. Manual changes don't sync with AIQUA's internal list and can cause:
> 
>   * Unsubscribed users to receive emails
>   * Inaccurate subscriber counts in segments
>

# Kakao (Chingu Talk)

Set up and launch Kakao campaigns.

Integrate your KakaoTalk channel to send targeted campaigns to your followers. Use AIQUA's audience segmentation and creative features to better personalize and optimize your messages.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes
> 
> AIQUA supports Chingu Talk for sending promotional messages, such as annual sale announcements, via Kakao campaigns. Alim Talk isn't supported.

![](https://files.readme.io/cf2fadf730f5ed287b8d422e1ed582f7427af9e47abfc926debab3c001652044-image_24_1.png)

Complete the following setup steps before you create your first Kakao Moment campaign:

  1. Connect your KakaoTalk channel
  2. Collect user phone numbers
  3. Launch and measure your campaigns



* * *

## 

1\. Connect your KakaoTalk channel

To send Kakao campaigns, integrate your KakaoTalk channel via Infobip:

  1. Verify that your KakaoTalk channel is connected to a Kakao business account and verified by Kakao.
  2. Contact [Infobip](https://www.infobip.com/docs/kakaotalk/getting-started) to create an Infobip account. Infobip will connect your Infobip account with your Kakao account and provide you with:
     * Access to the Infobip portal
     * Access to the WiseMOKA dashboard for uploading Kakao images
     * Your Kakao Sender Key
  3. Contact Appier Support at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#89ecfafad6fafcf9f9e6fbfdc9e8f9f9e0ecfba7eae6e4) and provide the following information to complete the configuration:
     * **Sender Key** : Your Kakao Sender Key from Infobip
     * **Base URL** : Found in [Infobip Portal > Home](https://portal.infobip.com/homepage/)
     * **API Key** : Found in [Infobip Portal > Home > Manage API Keys](https://portal.infobip.com/settings/accounts/api-keys)
  4. After configuration is complete, verify your integration status in the dashboard by selecting **Settings** > **Integration** > **Instant Messaging** > **Kakao**.

![](https://files.readme.io/228b0ef126cca991c59d1845d22f3c4a62b04721df928af7c65a6a59a60bf319-integration-kakao-chingu-talk.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Collect user phone numbers

Kakao campaigns require users to opt in to your KakaoTalk channel and have their phone numbers stored in the system. Before you launch a campaign, ensure user phone numbers are saved using the `phoneNo` attribute. You can collect this data using one of the following methods:

  * [Custom events and attributes](doc:custom-user-data#feature-specific-requirements): Work with your developers to log the phone number automatically when users interact with your site or app.
  * Upload: Import phone numbers manually [via the dashboard](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes) or programmatically [via the API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users).



* * *

## 

3\. Launch and measure your campaigns

After you complete your Kakao setup, you can create and monitor your campaigns.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you launch
> 
>   * Test your campaign by adding your device to the [test segment](doc:segments-test-segment#kakao-and-sms-campaigns) and using the **Send test creative** button to preview your campaign.
>   * **Blackout window** : Kakao Moment campaigns can't be sent from 9 PM to 8 AM Korea Standard Time (KST).
>   * [Dynamic content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives) isn't supported in Kakao campaigns.
> 


[ ![message campaign icon](https://files.readme.io/799b3b52556c6298544cde5d9622158e269d33942eec23c1411fe7bff784cb62-campaign-message.png) Create a Kakao campaign ](/docs/campaigns-message-create-kakao) [ ![Kakao creatives](https://files.readme.io/b33abe057f05b53ec7eb5da1a9879758c5e46e9170ae2f7c027e5e3809400705-KaKao_Talk.png) Design Kakao creatives ](/docs/creatives-kakao-chingutalk) [ ![View campaigns performance](https://files.readme.io/671763faf81485d7f4823a8371576ad34f686a56cc4bff9a5c19b98d5159fd08-Performance.png) View campaign performance ](/docs/campaigns-message-manage#view-campaign-performance)

# Kakao Moment

Set up and launch Kakao Moment campaigns.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you begin
> 
> You need a Kakao Business account with manager or admin permissions.

Connect your Kakao Moment account to send targeted campaigns to your KakaoTalk users. Use AIQUA's audience segmentation and creative features to better personalize and optimize your messages.

To ensure successful delivery, complete the following setup steps before you create your first Kakao Moment campaign:

  1. Connect your Kakao channel
  2. Collect user phone numbers
  3. Launch and measure your campaigns



* * *

## 

1\. Connect your Kakao channel

To send Kakao Moment campaigns, complete the following steps to integrate your Kakao Business account:

  1. Sign in to the [Kakao Business Console](https://business.kakao.com/), and invite Appier (`[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)`) as a manager to your Kakao Business account.
  2. Appier will create a Kakao Moment account for you. This process may take several days. After the account is created, accept the invitation under **Advertisement** > **Moment** in the **Requesting/Invited Advertising Accounts** tab, then add ad credits to your account.
  3. Complete one of the following based on your situation:
     * If your company doesn't have a Kakao developer app: Appier will create one for you. No additional action is required.
     * If your company already has a Kakao developer app: [Add `[email protected]` as a member with the **Editor** role](https://developers.kakao.com/docs/latest/en/app-setting/app#team-management) to enable Appier to onboard your app. After you've invited `[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)`, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#f7928484a884828787988583b79687879e9285d994989a)) to complete the integration.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Ad credits are required to run Kakao Moment campaigns from AIQUA.

* * *

## 

2\. Collect user phone numbers

Kakao Moment campaigns can only be sent to Kakao accounts linked to a Korean phone number. Before you launch a campaign, ensure user phone numbers are saved using the `phoneNo` attribute. You can collect this data using one of the following methods:

  * [Custom events and attributes](doc:custom-user-data#feature-specific-requirements): Work with your developers to log the phone number automatically when users interact with your site or app.
  * Upload: Import phone numbers manually [via the dashboard](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes) or programmatically [via the API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users).



* * *

## 

3\. Launch and measure your campaigns

After you complete your Kakao Moment setup, you can create and monitor your campaigns.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you launch
> 
>   * Test your campaign by adding your device to the [test segment](doc:segments-test-segment#kakao-and-sms-campaigns) and using the **Send test creative** button to preview your campaign.
>   * **Blackout window** : Kakao Moment campaigns can't be sent from 9 PM to 8 AM Korea Standard Time (KST).
>

# LINE

Set up and launch LINE campaigns.

Integrate your LINE official accounts with your AIQUA account to send targeted campaigns to your followers. Use audience segmentation and creative features to better personalize and optimize your messages.

To ensure successful delivery, complete the following setup steps before you create your first LINE campaign:

  1. Connect your LINE Official Account
  2. Sync LINE users
  3. Launch and measure your campaigns

![](https://files.readme.io/1eb3a62-LINECreatives.png)

* * *

## 

1\. Connect your LINE official account

AIQUA supports integration with the following [LINE official account types](https://www.linebiz.com/jp-en/service/line-official-account/account-type/):

  * LINE Premium Official Account
  * LINE Verified Official Account



To connect your LINE official account, enter your LINE channel credentials and contact Appier Support to complete the setup.

  1. In the dashboard, select your account name in the lower-left corner, then select **Integration** > **Instant Messaging** > **LINE**.

![](https://files.readme.io/7df822c9953f996aa7029f2f9909583d493fce0f350a9e337dd01e0c3a4c75f6-integration-line-aiqua.png)

  2. Select **Edit** , enter the following information, then select **Save** :


  * **Channel Name** : A name to identify this LINE channel.
  * **Channel ID** : Your LINE channel ID.
  * **Channel Secret** : Your LINE channel secret.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> How to get your LINE credentials
> 
> Sign in to your [LINE Official Account Manager](https://manager.line.biz), then select **Settings** > **Messaging API** to find your **Channel ID** and **Channel Secret**.

  3. Contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#f1948282ae828481819e8385b1908181989483df929e9c)) to complete the configuration. After configuration is complete, your LINE follower count appears on the integration page.

![](https://files.readme.io/dffe17819fb56bb7f285a9fc2488e9f9c745a32d344e1ffd6ad42e0fbd0e694e-followers.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> If you integrate other messaging services (such as third-party chatbot services) with the same LINE account credentials, the LINE API [rate limit](https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#rate-limits) is shared across all services. To control your send rate, use the [**Maximum notification send rate**](doc:user-settings#maximum-notification-send-rate) setting in the dashboard.

* * *

## 

2\. Sync LINE users

After you connect your LINE official account, a default segment called "[LINE]_LINE OA All Followers" is automatically created. This segment includes all current followers of your LINE channel and updates automatically as users follow or unfollow your account.

![](https://files.readme.io/6b9cbb7274f7be90398d075ee33b0970bd52d69f16cf148b729a9217ef5a0449-LINE_1.png)

To send [Trigger message campaign](doc:campaigns-message-create-line#campaign-type), you must configure [LINE User Sync](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync) to map LINE users with their existing web or app profiles. These messages are delivered only to mapped users.

* * *

## 

3\. Launch and measure your campaigns

After you complete your LINE setup, you can create and monitor your campaigns.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Test your campaign
> 
> Add your device to the [test segment](doc:segments-test-segment#line-campaigns) and use the **Send test creative** button to preview your campaign.

[ ![message campaign icon](https://files.readme.io/799b3b52556c6298544cde5d9622158e269d33942eec23c1411fe7bff784cb62-campaign-message.png) Create a LINE campaign ](/docs/campaigns-message-create-line) [ ![LINE creatives](https://files.readme.io/6f8c5d6d0080c21983ead56031718209b281c79f9ea13938ea8028ed591d5a83-LINE.png) Design LINE creatives ](/docs/creatives-line) [ ![View campaigns performance](https://files.readme.io/671763faf81485d7f4823a8371576ad34f686a56cc4bff9a5c19b98d5159fd08-Performance.png) View campaign performance ](/docs/campaigns-message-manage#view-campaign-performance)

To understand how users are counted in the LINE segment, see [LINE Segment FAQs](doc:line-segment-faqs).

# LINE User Sync

LINE user sync maps a user's LINE profile to their web or mobile profile in AIQUA. This synchronization allows you to use events captured on your website or mobile app to trigger personalized [LINE campaigns](doc:campaigns-message-create-line#campaign-type). You can sync users through three methods:

  * LINE creatives
  * LIFF URLs
  * Deep links



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
> Complete the following before configuring LINE user sync:
> 
>   * [Connect your LINE account](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line#1-connect-your-line-official-account).
>   * Web users: Integrate your website with the [Appier Web SDK](doc:integrating-with-the-aiqua-web-sdk).
>   * App users: Integrate your app with the Appier [Android](doc:android-sdk-overview) or [iOS](doc:ios-sdk-integration-overview) SDK.
>     * Android SDK 7.12.0 or later
>     * iOS SDK 7.20.0 or later
> 


* * *

## 

Sync via LINE creatives

This is the standard method for most LINE campaigns. When you add a **Destination URL** in [LINE Creatives](doc:creatives-line) that directs users to your website or app, the Appier SDK on your site detects the tracking parameter and syncs their profile with the web or mobile profile.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * No additional setup is required after the Web and Android SDK are integrated.
>   * To learn how to implement LINE user sync for iOS devices, see sync via Deep Links.
> 


* * *

## 

Sync via LIFF URLs

Use LINE Front-end Framework (LIFF) URLs to sync users directly from [LINE rich menus](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/using-rich-menus/#using-rich-menus-introduction), your website, or mobile app. Complete the following steps to create a LIFF app and generate a LIFF URL:

  1. [Create a LINE Login channel](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/line-login/getting-started/) and select **Web app** as the application type.
  2. In the LINE Developers Console, [link your LINE Official Account to LIFF app](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/line-login/link-a-bot/).
  3. [Configure the following settings for the LIFF app](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/liff/registering-liff-apps/#registering-liff-app):



Setting| Description  
---|---  
LIFF app name| Enter your LIFF app's name.  
Size| Select **Compact** to ensure that the LIFF browser only covers the bottom half of the device's screen. See the [LIFF docs](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/liff/overview#screen-size) for size references.  
Endpoint URL| Enter a placeholder URL, such as `https://appier.com` at this step.  
Scopes| Select **profile**.  
Add friend option| Select **On (aggressive)**.  
  
  4. Contact your customer success manager to request the LIFF Endpoint URL. Once received, go back to the LIFF tab and replace your placeholder URL with the actual URL.



### 

How to construct your LIFF URL

Construct the LIFF URL before you use it. The LIFF URL has the following format:
    
    
    https://liff.aiqua.appier.com/v2/<AIQUA APP ID>?dest=<ENCODED DESTINATION URL>&openExternalBrowser=1&mode=aggressive

  * `<AIQUA_APP_ID>`: Your Appier App ID (found in [Account Settings](doc:user-settings) on the dashboard).
  * `<ENCODED_DESTINATION_URL>`: The URL-encoded link where the user should be redirected (for example, `https%3A%2F%2Fwww.example.com`).
  * `&mode=aggressive`: Gives users the option to add your LINE Official Account after clicking on a LIFF app URL and logging in to their LINE account.



### 

LIFF app user sync flow

LIFF URLs can be used wherever links can be embedded, including your website, app, or LINE rich menu. Depending on where the LIFF URL is embedded, certain steps may differ slightly.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> Implementing LINE user sync using a LIFF app gives users the option to add your LINE Official Account, if they haven't done so already.

  1. The user clicks your LIFF URL.
  2. The user is then prompted to:  
i. Sign in to their LINE account (if the user isn't currently logged in to their LINE account) ii. Grant the LIFF app permission to access the user's LINE profile data iii. Add your LINE Official Channel (if the user hasn't already done so)
  3. After responding to the prompts, the user is redirected to the destination URL.
  4. If the user granted permission to the LIFF app, the user's LINE user ID is passed to the Appier SDK which then syncs the user's LINE profile data with the user's web or mobile profile. If the user didn't grant permission to the LIFF app, their profile is not synced.



* * *

## 

Sync via deep links

Deep links allow you to sync users who open your mobile app directly from a LINE campaign.

  * Android deep links: The Appier Android SDK automatically handles LINE user sync when a deep link opens the app. No additional configuration is required.
  * iOS deep links: The Appier iOS SDK requires configuration to handle deep links. Pass the following instructions to your development team. To enable sync on iOS, work with your development team using one of the following methods:
    * Manually handle iOS deep links in your app
    * Enable method swizzling



### 

Option 1: Handle iOS deep links in your app (Recommended)

Two types of URLs can be used to open your app: [URLs using a custom iOS URL scheme](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/defining-a-custom-url-scheme-for-your-app) and [universal links](https://developer.apple.com/ios/universal-links).

  1. To handle URLs using a custom iOS URL scheme: Call `handleOpenUrl()` in `application(_:,open:,options:)`
  2. To handle universal links: Call `handleUserActivity()` in `application(_:,continue:,restorationHandler:)`



The following code sample demonstrates how to properly call `handleOpenUrl()` and `handleUserActivity()`:

Swift
    
    
    func application(_ app: UIApplication, open url: URL, options: [UIApplication.OpenURLOptionsKey : Any] = [:]) -> Bool {
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().handleOpenUrl(url)
        ...
    }
    
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, continue userActivity: NSUserActivity, restorationHandler: @escaping ([UIUserActivityRestoring]?) -> Void) -> Bool {
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().handleUserActivity(userActivity)
        ...
    }

Objective-C
    
    
    - (BOOL)application:(UIApplication *)app openURL:(NSURL *)url options:(NSDictionary<NSString *,id> *)options {
        [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] handleOpenUrl:url];
        ...
    }
    
    - (BOOL)application:(UIApplication *)application continueUserActivity:(NSUserActivity *)userActivity restorationHandler:(void (^)(NSArray<id<UIUserActivityRestoring>> * _Nullable))restorationHandler {
        [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] handleUserActivity:userActivity];
        ...
    }

### 

Option 2: Enable method swizzling

When method swizzling is enabled in your app, the iOS SDK automatically handles LINE user syncing. For instructions on enabling method swizzling, see [Method Swizzling in the iOS SDK](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#enabling-method-swizzling).

# SMS/MMS

Set up and launch SMS/MMS campaigns.

You can integrate AIQUA with an SMS/MMS service provider to send text or multimedia messages to your users. Use AIQUA's audience segmentation and [dynamic content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives) features to better target your audience.

To ensure successful delivery and subscriber management, complete the following setup steps before creating your first SMS/MMS campaign:

  1. Connect with SMS/MMS service provider
  2. Collect user phone number
  3. Launch and measure your campaigns



* * *

## 

1\. Connect with SMS/MMS service provider

To send SMS/MMS campaigns, contact your customer success manager to connect your AIQUA account with the SMS/MMS service provider.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported regions for MMS and LMS
> 
>   * MMS: Only available in Taiwan.
>   * LMS: Only available in South Korea.
> 

> 
> Contact your customer success manager to learn more about enabling MMS or LMS for your account.

* * *

## 

2\. Collect user phone number

SMS/MMS campaigns can only be sent to users whose profiles include the `phoneNo` attribute. Before you launch a campaign, work with your developers to implement code that logs user phone numbers as the `phoneNo` user attribute. To learn more, see [Custom events and attributes](doc:custom-user-data#feature-specific-requirements).

* * *

## 

3\. Launch and measure your campaigns

After you complete your SMS/MMS setup, you can create and monitor your campaigns in AIQUA.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Test your campaign
> 
> Add your device to the [test segment](doc:segments-test-segment#kakao-and-sms-campaigns) and use the **Send test creative** button to preview your campaign.

# Web Push

Set up and launch web push campaigns.

Web push notifications are pop-up messages you can send to users in supported browsers even when they're not actively browsing your website. Use AIQUA's audience segmentation and [dynamic content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives) features to better personalize and optimize your messages.

![](https://files.readme.io/7caa2f5-WebPushStandard.png)

To ensure successful delivery and subscriber management, complete the following setup steps before creating your first web push campaign:

  1. Integrate the Web SDK
  2. Launch and monitor your campaigns



* * *

## 

1\. Integrate the Web SDK

Integrate your website with the Appier Web SDK to send web push campaigns. For detailed integration steps, see [Integrating the Appier Web SDK](doc:integrating-with-the-aiqua-web-sdk). If you're targeting Safari users, you must also complete [additional setup for Safari web push](doc:web-push-for-safari).

Once integrated, a system prompt will appear in the user's browser asking if they want to allow notifications. Users who click "Allow" will be subscribed to your web push notifications.

![](https://files.readme.io/f59996d-Screen_Shot_2020-03-20_at_1.49.27_PM.png)

### 

Supported browsers

Ensure your target audience uses compatible browsers and operating systems. Web push campaigns are supported on the following platforms:

Operating system| Supported browser and versions  
---|---  
Windows| • Chrome   
• Firefox  
MacOS| • Chrome   
• Safari 16.4 or later  
Android| • Chrome   
• Firefox  
iOS| Safari 16.4 or later  
iPadOS| Safari 16.4 or later  
  
> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * Safari (macOS, iOS, iPadOS) requires [additional setup](doc:web-push-for-safari).
>   * On iPadOS, web pages must be added to the home screen after completing the setup.
>   * Web push campaigns aren't supported on Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge browsers.
> 


* * *

## 

2\. Launch and monitor your campaigns

After you complete your web push setup, you can create and monitor your campaigns in AIQUA.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Test your campaign
> 
> Add your device to the [test segment](doc:segments-test-segment#web-push) and use the **Send test creative** button to preview your campaign.

[ ![Web Push Icon](https://files.readme.io/8bced4efae5c3f7c580b786e166a04edf687a871d7c7e08fd1080b2629d77ee9-Web_push.png) Create a push campaign ](/docs/campaigns-message-create-push) [ ![Web push creatives](https://files.readme.io/c209a0cb55d1ff9bfadb1fa19f0e1434a7260cf73c7bb43dd564fedae65d8cdb-Creative_templates.png) Design web push creatives ](/docs/creatives-web-push) [ ![View campaigns performance](https://files.readme.io/671763faf81485d7f4823a8371576ad34f686a56cc4bff9a5c19b98d5159fd08-Performance.png) View campaign performance ](/docs/campaigns-regular-manage#view-campaign-performance)

# Known Issues

Here are the known issues for web push.

  * Web push doesn't show on macOS 10.15 (Catalina) with Chrome
  * Web push is no longer supported in incognito or private browsing
  * HTTP web push limitation for macOS Chrome
  * HTTP-integrated sites can't identify if a site was removed
  * Web page doesn't load when clicking a web push from Action Center



* * *

## 

Web push doesn't show on macOS 10.15 (Catalina) with Chrome

Previously, some users using macOS 10.15 (Catalina) are not able to receive web push on Chrome. This issue has since been resolved by Chrome version 78.0.3904.97. MacOS users experiencing problems with web push can upgrade their Chrome browser to the latest version.

* * *

## 

Web push is no longer supported in incognito or private browsing

Due to a [Chrome update](https://www.blog.google/outreach-initiatives/google-news-initiative/protecting-private-browsing-chrome/), Appier SDK can no longer support the web push feature in Incognito mode.

Following this update, if you're sending a web push notification, these are the possible fake prompt scenarios when a user uses Chrome or Firefox for browsing.

Browser| Browsing mode| Web protocol| Fake prompt scenario  
---|---|---|---  
Chrome| Incognito| HTTP| Fake prompt and dialog appear, but dialog gets automatically closed  
Chrome| Incognito| HTTPS| No fake prompt  
Chrome| Regular| HTTP| Fake prompt and system prompt with dialog appear  
Chrome| Regular| HTTPS| Fake prompt and system prompt appear  
Firefox| Private| HTTP| No fake prompt  
Firefox| Private| HTTPS| No fake prompt  
Firefox| Regular| HTTP| Fake prompt and system prompt with dialog appear  
Firefox| Regular| HTTPS| Fake prompt and system prompt appear  
  
* * *

## 

HTTP web push limitation for macOS Chrome

Date| Status  
---|---  
06/05/2019| Chrome browser, used on a macOS device, trims a subdomain name that exceeds 10 characters. This is a third-party system limitation.  
  
* * *

## 

HTTP-integrated sites can't identify if a site was removed

Date| Status  
---|---  
05/31/2019| Due to a [Chrome update](https://www.chromestatus.com/feature/6451284559265792), an HTTP-integrated Appier web SDK can't track if a domain was manually removed. The Appier web SDK isn't allowed to do permission checks via iFrame and can only get cache results from the notify domain.  
06/03/2019| Won't fix.  
  
* * *

## 

Web page doesn't load when clicking a web push from Action Center

Date| Status  
---|---  
03/23/2019| The issue was identified as happening across Chrome browsers running on Windows 10. We are currently tracking third-party updates and testing for a possible workaround. For more details on this issue, see this [reference](https://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/forum/all/google-chrome-notifications-in-windows-action/999eb370-568b-4861-be1e-98a09a443190?page=3).

# In-App Campaigns

Learn how to create in-app campaigns.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you begin
> 
> To deliver in-app campaigns, you must integrate the [Appier SDK](doc:sdk-getting-started) with your Android or iOS app.

In-app campaigns display notifications to users while they're active in your mobile app. Unlike push notifications that appear on the device lock screen, in-app campaigns appear only when users are engaged with your application. You can trigger these campaigns based on user events collected by the Appier SDK.

  * To learn how to create a campaign, see [Create an in-app campaign](doc:campaigns-in-app-create).
  * After creating campaigns, you can [manage them from the campaign list](doc:campaigns-in-app-manage).

![](https://files.readme.io/f2e4cc34c0cd1c09a79b0f3f28639cf7f8642089d6a2dc59d1b37a21b5be7a04-In-app--.png)

* * *

## 

Campaign types

There are two types of in-app campaigns:

Campaign type| Description  
---|---  
**Pop-up**|  Display notifications when users are actively viewing your app. You can design in-app pop-up using [basic templates](doc:creatives-in-app-basic-templates), [Creative Studio](doc:creative-studio), and the [HTML editor](doc:creatives-in-app-html-editor).  
**Inbox**|  Display offers or notify users of important updates without sending them push notifications.   
  
This is a beta feature and requires additional SDK integration. For more information, see:  
• [Inbox Notifications for Android](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-android)  
• [Inbox Notifications for iOS](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-ios)  
  
* * *

## 

Limitations

### 

SDK version requirements

Some features require specific SDK versions:

Feature| iOS SDK| Android SDK| React Native SDK| Additional requirements  
---|---|---|---|---  
[**Audience**](doc:campaigns-in-app-create#audience) settings: **New users** segment| 7.11.0| 7.1.0| —| —  
[**Audience**](doc:campaigns-in-app-create#optional-segment-by-events-in-the-last-24-hours) settings: Segment by events in the last 24 hours| 7.15.0| 7.6.0| 1.7.0| Contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#a4c1d7d7fbd7d1d4d4cbd6d0e4c5d4d4cdc1d68ac7cbc9)) to enable it for your account.  
[**Real-time trigger**](doc:campaigns-in-app-create#real-time-trigger): `first_app_launched` trigger| 7.11.0| 7.1.0| —| —  
[**Campaign settings**](doc:campaigns-in-app-create#campaign-settings): Daily frequency cap| 5.1.0| 5.8.2| —| —  
  
### 

Campaign priority

  * In-app campaigns in [journey maps](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/getting-started-with-journey-maps) automatically have higher priority than standalone in-app campaigns.
  * Campaigns that use Creative Studio don't follow priority-based positioning. By default, they appear below basic creatives. To change this default setting, contact Appier Support.

# Manage In-App Campaigns

You can view and manage your in-app campaigns from the campaign list (**Campaigns > In-app campaigns**). In addition to searching and filtering existing campaigns, you can perform operations such as turning on campaigns, viewing the campaign's performance page, and exporting reports.

  * Search and filter campaigns
  * Perform campaign operations
  * View campaign performance

![](https://files.readme.io/7c19bad228489c0a070b0c26eceb9ba08db611a6f081883295940f98654cf2c4-in-app-campaign-manage.png)

* * *

## 

Search and filter campaigns

From the campaign list, you can search campaigns and apply various filters to view a more focused set of campaigns.

### 

Search

Enter search terms to find campaigns by name or ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/83b455f5a1ea4dc8583c5c2433b7253c0e57a05ab3b0af1e0a11f0c6557da94d-in-app-search.png)

### 

Filter

Use the provided filter options to streamline campaign list results.

![](https://files.readme.io/bb3f6dba05fb9f5d6422881988279166a5207898dfdd36b474f2d5712b55ede6-in-app-filter.png)

Filter option| Description  
---|---  
**Channel**|  Select a campaign channel, either **Android** or **iOS**.  
**Status**|  Select one of the following campaign statuses:  
  
• **Draft** : The campaign hasn't been sent yet.  
• **Scheduled** : The campaign is scheduled to run in the future.  
• **Active** : The campaign has been turned on.  
• **Completed** : The campaign period has ended.  
• **Inactive** : The campaign was manually turned off before it's campaign delivery window has passed.  
• **Archived** : The campaign has been archived.  
**Tag**|  Select one or more tags from the dropdown.  
  
* * *

## 

Perform campaign operations

From the campaign list, you can access campaign actions by clicking the three vertical dots next to the campaign's name.

![](https://files.readme.io/ba3ec5e025ee859a508cf5d1771e72137025619d6f53f976e6fc959392590142-in-app-actions.png)

The following table describes the operations available for in-app campaigns.

Campaign operation| Description  
---|---  
**Duplicate**|  Duplicate the campaign. The duplicated campaign's name will be the original campaign's name with "`-copy`" appended.  
**Modify tags**|  Add and remove tags for this campaign.  
**View Activity Logs**|  View logs detailing operations performed on this campaign.  
**Export user report**|  Export a user report containing data about users who interacted with or received this campaign.  
**Export form data**|  Only available for lead generation campaigns. Specify an email to receive a report that contains the information submitted by the users in the lead form.  
  
If you've enabled experiments in a lead generation campaign, the information collected from each variant will be a separate tab in the [downloaded file](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-download-form-data-in-web-in-app).  
  
The `submitTime` of the lead form is based on the timezone set in your [account settings](doc:user-settings).  
**Archive**|  Archive the campaign. Archived campaigns aren't displayed in the campaign list unless the status filter is set to include campaigns with the **Archived** status.  
  
### 

Enable and disable campaigns

In-app campaigns can be enabled and disabled from the campaign list. Only campaigns with an **Active** status will be sent when trigger conditions are met.

![](https://files.readme.io/d53d50a9059391f1c5b544cf10d2414fa20ba14ceb4919d1f23e85d8779fb460-in-app-toggle.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Disabling and re-enabling a campaign resets the [**Frequency cap**](doc:campaigns-in-app-create#frequency-cap) for users who opened the app while the campaign was disabled. Users who didn't open the app retain their frequency cap counter.

* * *

## 

View campaign performance

You can view performance data using:

  * Campaign list metrics
  * The campaign's performance page
  * Exportable reports



### 

Campaign list metrics

![](https://files.readme.io/55a89016d6daaf9eaec016f4a571c253f285f73ba873436ae15cefbc62376a56-in-app-metrics.png)

The following table lists the metrics and campaign details visible from the campaign list.

Metric| Description  
---|---  
**Submissions**|  The number of campaign forms submitted in lead generation campaigns. This is based on the number of `qg_inweb_lead_gen` events.  
**Impressions**|  An impression is counted when a user receives a campaign notification on their device. This is based on the number of `notification_received` events.  
  
For example, if the campaign is sent to an audience with 50K users, and only 30K users receive it on their devices, then the number of impressions is 30K.  
**Clicks**|  The total number of clicks on the campaign based on the number of `notification_clicked` events.  
**Conv. count**|  The count of online conversion events until the campaign's end date. This is based on the attribution settings and conversion events you selected in your account settings.  
**Conv. value**|  The monetary value associated with online conversion events.  
  
For example, if the conversion event is `checkout_completed`, the **Conv. value** represents the sum of the conversion values of all `checkout_completed` events attributed to the campaign.  
**Offline conv. count**|  The count of offline conversion events uploaded through [Offline Event API v2](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2). This is based on the attribution settings you selected in your account settings.  
**Offline conv. value**|  The monetary value of all offline conversion events attributed to the campaign.  
**Trigger rule**|  The campaign [trigger](doc:campaigns-in-web-create#real-time-trigger).  
**Start date**|  The start date of the campaign delivery schedule.  
**End date**|  The end date of the campaign delivery schedule.  
**Include segments**|  Segments selected to receive this campaign. Hover over this column to view the full list of included segments.  
**Exclude segments**|  Segments excluded from receiving this campaign. Hover over this column to view the full list of excluded segments.  
**Last edited**|  The last time the campaign was edited.  
  
### 

Campaign performance page

Click on the campaign's name to open its performance page. For details about an individual campaign's performance page, see [View Performance](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance).

![](https://files.readme.io/ba39b78b2cf2734f93063d93f0a71fb04202bb058f4519e79dd678abcca44607-in-app-individual-campaign.png)

### 

Exportable reports

  * Campaign performance report
  * User report



#### 

Campaign performance report

Campaign performance reports contain campaign details and performance metrics, and can be exported to a CSV file and downloaded via URL sent to your email address. To learn more about what data the campaign performance report includes, see [Export Campaign Performance Reports](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-export-campaign-performance-reports).

To export a campaign performance report, click **Export report**.

![](https://files.readme.io/0d4d8c38c6dbb44ee5c96c1bb7b747fa007398dbb4f254d98842fb69d5a1e987-in-app-campaign-export.png)

#### 

User report

User reports contain data about users who interacted with or received this campaign, including their user ID, email address, and whether they performed certain actions, such as opens and clicks. The report can be exported to a CSV file and downloaded via URL sent to your email address. For more details about the data contained in user reports, see [Export Campaign User Reports](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-export-campaign-user-reports).

To export this report, click the three vertical dots to open the list of available campaign actions, then click **Export user report**.

![](https://files.readme.io/fd2dc04ccae91f5ac63929f201b1b4f5d6bfd197d2ae07496511efcdb10b82e6-in-app-user-report.png)

# In-Web Campaigns

Send in-web campaigns.

In-web campaigns display notifications to users on your website. You can trigger these campaigns based on user actions, how far users scroll, inactivity, or when users attempt to leave the page.

  * To learn how to create a campaign, see [Create an in-web campaign](doc:campaigns-in-web-create).
  * After creating campaigns, you can [manage them from the campaign list](doc:campaigns-in-web-manage).

![1103](https://files.readme.io/bd10366-in-web_campaign_overview.png)

* * *

## 

Integration requirements

Before you can use in-web campaigns, you must complete the following setup steps:

  1. Integrate the SDK. Connect your website with [Appier Web SDK](doc:web-sdk-overview).
  2. Enable in-web notifications. Go to **Settings** > **Integration** > **Website** and select **Enable In-Web Notification**.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> To ensure in-web creatives display correctly on mobile devices, add the following meta tag to the `<head>` element of your website. This tag helps the browser adjust content to fit the user's device screen.
> 
> `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`

* * *

## 

Guidelines and limitations

  * Campaign display
  * Technical considerations



### 

Campaign display

  * When multiple campaigns trigger simultaneously, the system displays them according to the [display type and campaign priority](doc:campaigns-in-web-create#campaign-settings) settings. Each campaign counts one impression, even if another campaign overlays it and the user can't see it.
  * Priority exceptions apply to the following campaign types:
    * In-web campaigns in journey maps automatically have higher priority than standalone in-web campaigns.
    * Campaign priority settings don't apply to campaigns using **Creative Studio**. By default, **Creative Studio** campaigns appear below campaigns created with [basic templates](doc:creatives-in-web-basic-templates). To adjust this setting, contact Appier Support.



### 

Technical considerations

  * When viewing an in-web campaign after enabling or editing it, open a new tab or window in your browser instead of refreshing an existing tab. If you refresh an existing tab, the updated campaign might not appear for up to five minutes due to browser caching.
  * If your website is a single page application (SPA), campaigns remain on screen when users navigate to different pages because the webpage doesn't reload during navigation. Users must manually close the campaign.

# Create an In-Web Campaign

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you begin
> 
> Complete the [Web SDK integration](doc:web-sdk-overview) before creating a campaign.

To create an in-web campaign, go to **Campaigns > In-web campaigns**, then click **\+ Create campaign**.

![](https://files.readme.io/843e1269d9ba8f42f53317d1e3e81ecb25126f470fcf28ad284c9abb4e31c9a3-in-web-campaigns-create.png)

Next, complete the campaign settings.

  1. Audience: Set campaign info and choose your audience.
  2. Creative: Design campaign creatives and variants.
  3. Settings: Set campaign-level settings, such as the schedule and campaign goals.
  4. Review and launch: Confirm your settings before launching.



* * *

## 

1\. Set campaign info and choose your audience

Enter your campaign's basic information, select your audience, and add a trigger rule.

### 

Campaign info

Enter a campaign name and select the devices you want to display this campaign to. In addition, you have the option to add:

  * Tags which can be used for filtering in the [campaign list](doc:campaigns-in-web-manage).
  * A campaign description.

![](https://files.readme.io/b8665d410e69def5bee813ae79fbd87a49d91f076a81669eb8b719ecc445ce08-in-web-audience.png)

### 

Audience

Under **Audience** , select which user segments to include in or exclude from your campaign.

Setting| Description  
---|---  
**Users to include**|  Specifies which users receive the campaign. You can select up to 10 segments.  
  
• If you don't select a segment, the campaign targets all default web users, including users who visited within the last 24 hours.  
• **New users** : Select this segment to target web users who first visited your website within the last 24 hours.  
• Other segments: Users appear in these segments up to 24 hours after they meet the segment conditions.  
**Users to exclude**|  Specifies which users don't receive the campaign. You can select up to 10 segments.  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/bd92e0ab1a47ce304221200a2123436d5b66d9b8837ece97cc6d4fc511dd12e8-in-web-audiences-all-users.png)

To target users based on specific events that occurred within the last 24 hours, enable **Segment by events in the last 24 hours**.

#### 

(Optional) Segment by events in the last 24 hours

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes
> 
>   * This is a beta feature. While this feature is currently available for use, you may encounter occasional bugs or stability issues.
>   * This feature doesn't work across multiple domains or subdomains. Use regular user segmentation for cross-domain tracking. For more information, see [Cross-domain integration](doc:cross-domain-integration).
> 


To target audiences based on recent activity, enable **Segment by events in the last 24 hours**. This feature refines your audience based on events users completed within the last 24 hours. Configure the following settings:

  * **Include users who completed** : Narrows your audience to users who completed specific events. Select whether users must complete **any** or **all** of the selected events, then select **\+ Add event** to choose which events to track.
  * **Exclude users who completed** : Removes users who completed specific events from your audience. Select whether to exclude users who completed **any** or **all** of the selected events, then select **\+ Add event** to choose which events to track.
  * **In the last** : Sets the time window for when events occurred. Enter a value in minutes or hours (must be less than 24 hours).

![](https://files.readme.io/bf087539218dc6b2ab25e67ff9b3300cbc71a668f103cd0f439fa260240c9a89-segment-by-events-last-24-hours.png)

### 

Real-time trigger

Under **Rule** , select a trigger rule that determines when to display your campaign to users who meet your targeting criteria. You can also exclude specific URLs to prevent the campaigns from displaying on certain pages.

![](https://files.readme.io/ff8634ec88e0263a0c6ca8aa744cb7916459d869d161fb8fffd65cd4082cdbaa-real-time-trigger.png)

Rule| Description| Usage  
---|---|---  
**User action**|  Triggers your campaign when users perform a specific action tracked as a [user event](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/user-data-collection#user-events). You can configure the campaign to display immediately or after a specified delay.| Send a notification that respond to specific user behaviors, such as adding items to a cart, completing a form, or clicking a button.  
**Scroll percentage**|  Triggers your campaign when users scroll to a specified percentage of the page. Set the scroll threshold between 10% and 100%.  
  
• Select **Add event property** to specify which pages trigger this campaign.  
• The campaign displays only once per user session. Each time a user opens your website in a new tab or window counts as a new session.| Send a notification to engage users who are actively reading content or to capture attention after users view key information.  
**Idle time**|  Triggers your campaign when users remain inactive for a specified duration. Set the idle threshold between 10 seconds and 10 minutes.  
  
• Select **Add event property** to specify which pages trigger this campaign.  
• On mobile devices, users must interact with the page before the idle timer starts. The timer stops when the browser moves to the background.| Send a notification to re-engage users who appear distracted or to offer assistance when users pause while browsing.  
**Exit intent**|  Triggers your campaign when users move their cursor toward the top of the browser window, indicating intent to leave the page.  
  
• Select **Add event property** to specify which pages trigger this campaign.  
• The campaign displays only once per user session. Each time a user opens your website in a new tab or window counts as a new session.  
• This trigger doesn't work on mobile browsers.| Send a notification to retain users before they leave, such as offering discounts, capturing email addresses, or highlighting key features.  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Limitations
> 
>   * The `first_visited` virtual event can't be used as a trigger rule.
>   * User events uploaded through the API can't be used as trigger rules.
> 


#### 

(Optional) Exclude URLs

Enable **Exclude URLs** to prevent notifications from appearing on specific pages. For example, you might want to disable notifications on checkout pages to avoid distracting users during purchase completion.

Select how to match URLs:

  * **Equals** : Disables notifications from the exact URL you enter.
  * **Contains** : Disables notifications from all URLs containing the text you enter.



Click **\+ Add URL** to exclude additional URLs.

![](https://files.readme.io/8bf7dbe4aca96350dae9bce4b563388f2a09b04f7e0f33d7d4c558d6ae205e9a-rules-exclude-urls.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> URLs can only contain ASCII characters. Non-English characters (for example, Chinese or Japanese characters) aren't supported.

* * *

## 

2\. Set up creatives

Under **Creative** , click **\+ Select template** , and select how you'd like to add the creative. For details about basic templates and the different ways to create one, see [In-Web Creatives](doc:creatives-in-web).

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Creative Studio browser support
> 
> In-web campaigns designed with Creative Studio aren't supported on Internet Explorer, Safari, and any browsers in incognito mode. To learn more about devices compatibility, see [Browser compatibility](doc:creatives-in-web#browser-compatibility).

[ ![Basic templates](https://files.readme.io/859fc5991e739d7c1741680b820bf38e9dcad1b723c47f09f11ac621513f4765-In-web_Campaign.png) Basic templates ](/docs/creatives-in-web-basic-templates) [ ![HTML Editor](https://files.readme.io/41bc293e71ecd0cce22bd2feb9349cfeadaa176db2c5aacff2800cea3bb37e35-HTML_editor.png) HTML editor ](/docs/creatives-in-web-html-editor) [ ![Creative Studio](https://files.readme.io/41adb8973ff0bf7945324ef1ced106d187a24e48c117bd582dab9af3cbfffa05-Creative_templates.png) Creative Studio ](/docs/creative-studio)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Experiments
> 
> Set up campaign experiments to compare different creative variants and measure campaign effectiveness. For details, see [Experiments: In-web](doc:campaigns-experiments-in-web-and-in-app).

In addition, you can generate a preview link to see how your creative appears on your website. To learn more, see [Preview on website](doc:creatives-in-web#preview-on-website). After setting up the creative, click **Next** to finalize your campaign's settings.

* * *

## 

3\. Configure campaign settings

  * Under **Schedule**, choose how and when to send the campaign.
  * Under **Campaign settings**, configure campaign-level settings, such as campaign's goals and frequency cap.



### 

Schedule

In the **Schedule** section, set the **Start date** and **End date** of your in-web campaign.

![](https://files.readme.io/244ebf9e93c2cf06998e34a5fb87e6ebe70bbbbeca999608a6a4fcc0d3c7d140-settings-schedule.png)

### 

Campaign settings

Under the **Campaign settings** section, configure when and how often to display your campaign.

Setting| Description  
---|---  
**Frequency cap**|  Controls how often users see the campaign:  
  
• **Show repeatedly** : Displays the campaign multiple times, up to the specified limit.  
• **Show only once in the user 's lifetime**: Displays the campaign only once during the campaign period.  
**Must display**|  When selected, this campaign always displays when conditions are met, even if other campaigns are triggered simultaneously. Use this for fixed banners that don't block the main page content.  
  
When not selected, only one standard campaign displays if multiple standard campaigns are triggered at the same time.  
**Campaign priority**|  Determines which campaigns appear when multiple campaigns are triggered simultaneously. Use a lower priority number to display a higher campaign priority.  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/b3050aa5e5655a5528d96f28058186a9eecbe41aeb6d215a32dcec20310668d5-in-web-campigns-settings.png)

#### 

How multiple campaigns display

When multiple campaigns are triggered at the same time:

  1. All campaigns with **Must display** selected appear on the page.
  2. Only one standard campaign with the highest priority (lowest number) appears.
  3. Campaigns appear in priority order from top to bottom (lower numbers display higher on the page)



For example, if campaigns with priorities 1, 3, and 10 are all must-display campaigns triggered simultaneously, they appear stacked with priority 1 at the top, priority 3 in the middle, and priority 10 at the bottom.

![](https://files.readme.io/d2bdc6d-Screen_Shot_2021-08-02_at_6.33.51_PM.png)

For information about priority exceptions and additional display behaviors, see [Guidelines and limitations](doc:campaigns-in-web#guidelines-and-limitations).

* * *

## 

4\. Review and launch

Finally, review and confirm your campaign settings. When you're ready to launch the campaign, click **Save**.

![](https://files.readme.io/3e78b0ceff0224961b5c0d57d2e2a9306fa6ceeac6b3fe47dc442cec7b71d277-preview-in-web.png)

In-web campaigns need to be enabled manually from the campaign list to go live. Note that after you have enabled a campaign for the first time, the creative type can no longer be changed.

![](https://files.readme.io/2c3ab06021c771f3f48bb978e1d491e5a0f452855e39cab2f9e19063358e2c5b-in-web-campaigns-toggle.png)

* * *

## 

Use cases

  * Target inactive app users
  * Target users with items in cart
  * Encourage users to log in



### 

Target inactive app users

Send campaigns to users who haven't opened your mobile app recently. The campaign can be set up as below:

  * **Users to include** : Keep the default (**All users**)
  * **Users to exclude** : Select a segment containing users who opened the app in the last 30 days



### 

Target users with items in cart

Remind users who recently added items to their shopping cart but are leaving without purchasing. The campaign can be set up as below:

  * **Users to include** : Keep the default (**All users**)
  * **Segment by events in the last 24 hours** : Enable
    * **Include users who completed** : `product_added_to_cart`
    * **Exclude users who completed** : `checkout_completed`
    * **In the last** : 24 hours
  * **Real-time trigger** : **Exit intent**



### 

Encourage users to log in

Show members-only discount notifications to users who are browsing without logging in. The campaign can be set up as below:

  * **Users to include** : Keep the default (**All users**)
  * **Segment by events in the last 24 hours** : Enable
    * **Include users who completed** : `product_viewed`
      * **Where total count** `>` "5"
    * **Exclude users who completed** : `login`
    * **In the last** : 2 hours
  * **Real-time trigger** : **User action**
    * **Show the notification when the user does** : `page_viewed`

# Manage In-Web Campaigns

You can view and manage your in-web campaigns from the campaign list (**Campaigns > In-web campaigns**). In addition to searching and filtering existing campaigns, you can perform operations such as turning on campaigns, viewing the campaign's performance page, and exporting reports.

  * Search and filter campaigns
  * Perform campaign operations
  * View campaign performance

![](https://files.readme.io/3b71af13391f769a382e8fb80f97495453bdfc935579d8cad1cb49c7b101157a-in-web-campaigns-manage.png)

* * *

## 

Search and filter campaigns

From the campaign list, you can search campaigns and apply various filters to view a more focused set of campaigns.

### 

Search

Enter search terms to find campaigns by name or ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/699ccb96c4f6c3381de544bc6b86fea169d95308e0ab85e66c57fb82a625f17b-in-web-search.png)

### 

Filter

Use the provided filter options to streamline campaign list results.

![](https://files.readme.io/a64c6a89cf08588d3b58d2c8057cc649698603bcd6413a2bb563855d7c873c1b-in-web-filter.png)

Filter option| Description  
---|---  
**Status**|  Select one of the following campaign statuses:  
  
• **Draft** : The campaign hasn't been sent yet.  
• **Scheduled** : The campaign is scheduled to run in the future.  
• **Active** : The campaign has been turned on.  
• **Completed** : The campaign period has ended.  
• **Inactive** : The campaign was manually turned off before it's campaign delivery window has passed.  
• **Archived** : The campaign has been archived.  
**Device**|  Select a campaign targeted device, either **All** , **Android** , **iOS** , or **PC and other devices**.  
**Tag**|  Select one or more tags from the dropdown.  
**Trigger rule**|  Select one or more campaign trigger rules.  
  
* * *

## 

Perform campaign operations

From the campaign list, you can access campaign actions by clicking the three vertical dots next to the campaign's name.

![](https://files.readme.io/c5c90abafb3cb8d495e759d2679083d2a3c63e4159d3be30e33e97320b1542e4-in-web-actions.png)

The following table describes the operations available for in-web campaigns.

Campaign operation| Description  
---|---  
**Duplicate**|  Duplicate the campaign. The duplicated campaign's name will be the original campaign's name with "`-copy`" appended.  
**Modify tags**|  Add and remove tags for this campaign.  
**View Activity Logs**|  View logs detailing operations performed on this campaign.  
**Export user report**|  Export a user report containing data about users who interacted with or received this campaign.  
**Export form data**|  Only available for lead generation campaigns. Specify an email to receive a report that contains the information submitted by the users in the lead form.  
  
If you've enabled experiments in a lead generation campaign, the information collected from each variant will be a separate tab in the [downloaded file](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-download-form-data-in-web-in-app).  
  
The `submitTime` of the lead form is based on the timezone set in your [account settings](doc:user-settings).  
**Archive**|  Archive the campaign. Archived campaigns aren't displayed in the campaign list unless the status filter is set to include campaigns with the **Archived** status.  
  
### 

Enable and disable campaigns

In-web campaigns can be enabled and disabled from the campaign list. Only campaigns with an **Active** status will be sent when trigger conditions are met.

![](https://files.readme.io/f3b6a2eb59fc21838ab6c24a0d547650f9efe062b9c774f6a7126ffdb5ed6dd8-in-web-status.png)

* * *

## 

View campaign performance

You can view performance data using:

  * Campaign list metrics
  * The campaign's performance page
  * Exportable reports



### 

Campaign list metrics

![](https://files.readme.io/0d3576b2e304bbf8db2e6a0d806f11dfc9d2ed55a0862f7da34861cc63b0598f-in-web-list-metrics.png)

The following table lists the metrics and campaign details visible from the campaign list.

Metric| Description  
---|---  
**Status**|  The current status of the campaign, one of: **Draft** , **Scheduled** , **Active** , **Completed** , **Inactive** , or **Archived**.  
**Priority**|  The campaign's [display priority](doc:campaigns-in-web-create#campaign-settings).  
**Device**|  The target device types selected for the in-web campaign.  
**Submissions**|  The number of campaign forms submitted in lead generation campaigns. This is based on the number of `qg_inweb_lead_gen` events.  
**Impressions**|  An impression is counted when a user receives a campaign notification on their device. This is based on the number of `qg_inweb_displayed` events.  
**Clicks**|  The total number of clicks and form submissions in the campaign. This is based on the count for `qg_inweb_clicked` and `qg_inweb_lead_gen` events which are logged under the following conditions:  
  
• Basic template (Lead generation): When the user submits a lead generation form.  
• Basic template (Subscription boost): When the user clicks to allow push notifications.  
• Basic template (Fixed banner): When the user clicks on the action button.  
• Basic template (Multiple Images): When the user clicks on an image or action button.  
• Basic template (Multiple actions): When the user clicks on an action button where the **Click action** is set to **Open URL**.  
• Creative Studio: When the user clicks on a creative element where element's **Action** is set to **URL** and when the user submits a form by clicking on a creative element where the element's **Action** is set to **Submit form**.  
**Conv. count**|  The count of online conversion events until the campaign's end date. This is based on the attribution settings and conversion events you selected in your account settings.  
**Conv. value**|  The monetary value associated with online conversion events.For example, if the conversion event is `checkout_completed`, the **Conv. value** represents the sum of the conversion values of all `checkout_completed` events attributed to the campaign.  
**Offline conv. count**|  The count of offline conversion events uploaded through [Offline Event API v2](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2). This is based on the attribution settings you selected in your account settings.  
**Offline conv. value**|  The monetary value of all offline conversion events attributed to the campaign.  
**Trigger rule**|  The campaign [trigger](doc:campaigns-in-web-create#real-time-trigger).  
**Start date**|  The start date of the campaign delivery schedule.  
**End date**|  The end date of the campaign delivery schedule.  
**Include segments**|  Segments selected to receive this campaign. Hover over this column to view the full list of included segments.  
**Exclude segments**|  Segments excluded from receiving this campaign. Hover over this column to view the full list of excluded segments.  
**Last edited**|  The last time the campaign was edited.  
  
### 

Campaign performance page

Click on the campaign's name to open its performance page. For details about an individual campaign's performance page, see [View Performance](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance).

![](https://files.readme.io/50f115138458078c938e06b87f7df580ed9fdb6cea4730801be14a48a2aebfa8-in-web-campaign-performance.png)

### 

Exportable reports

  * Campaign performance report
  * User report



#### 

Campaign performance report

Campaign performance reports contain campaign details and performance metrics, and can be exported to a CSV file and downloaded via URL sent to your email address. To learn more about what data the campaign performance report includes, see [Export Campaign Performance Reports](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-export-campaign-performance-reports).

To export a campaign performance report, click **Export report**.

![](https://files.readme.io/ecd230c4e820d9ba3cc07a18b11a1b2bcfe574502faed6ad88d780fa94bf0a17-in-web-export-report.png)

#### 

User report

User reports contain data about users who interacted with or received this campaign, including their user ID, email address, and whether they performed certain actions, such as opens and clicks. The report can be exported to a CSV file and downloaded via URL sent to your email address. For more details about the data contained in user reports, see [Export Campaign User Reports](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-export-campaign-user-reports).

To export this report, click the three vertical dots to open the list of available campaign actions, then click **Export user report**.

![](https://files.readme.io/53fe34d7acf4ccb47dab18a1a62aa93773a999f054aaddeb168ddc53be812377-in-web-export-user-report.png)

# Message Campaigns

Send push, email, and instant message campaigns.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Before you begin
> 
> See [Getting Started with Campaigns](doc:campaigns-getting-started) to learn how to set up and enable each marketing channel before creating your first campaign.

Message campaigns allow you to send push (web and app), email, and instant message (LINE, Kakao Moment, Kakao Chingu Talk) to your users.

  * To learn how to create a regular campaigns, see [Create a Message Campaign](doc:campaigns-message-create).
  * After creating campaigns, you can [manage them from the campaign list](doc:campaigns-message-manage).



* * *

## 

Message campaign features

You can enhance the effectiveness and improve engagement for your email and push campaigns using campaign experiments or send time optimization.

### 

Campaign experiments

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported channels and campaign types
> 
>   * Email (regular campaigns)
>   * Push (regular campaigns)
> 


Experiments allow you to conduct A/B test to identify which campaign creatives are most effective, allowing you to optimize for campaign impact. [Experiments](doc:campaigns-experiments-message) are supported for push and email campaigns.

![](https://files.readme.io/6161cd29e5e4653ff1d0ec8b46e2b97d2dc584578dea197412e96a5705016266-regular-campaigns-experiments.png)

### 

Send time optimization

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported channels and campaign types
> 
>   * Email (regular campaigns)
>   * Push (regular campaigns)
> 


Send time optimization uses AIQUA's AI to determine the most optimal send time in the 24-hour period following the campaign's scheduled send time to maximize engagement. The 24-hour sending window is based on your account's [time zone setting](doc:user-settings#timezone)).

  * **Personalized targeting** : The actual send time is uniquely optimized for each user, considering individual behavior and overall engagement trends to determine the optimal send time.
  * **Real-time learning** : AIQUA's AI continually learns and updates its definition of what's optimal based on new engagement data.
  * **Built-in safeguards to reduce bias** : Unlike simpler rule-based systems, AIQUA's send time optimization ensures training data isn’t skewed by past, manually scheduled campaigns. In addition, self-balancing systems prevent feedback loops caused by the AI training on its own past behavior. These safeguards ensure optimization decisions are based solely on user behavior.



To enable send time optimization:

  1. Under **Schedule** , select **One-time schedule**.
  2. Check **Enable send time optimization**.

![](https://files.readme.io/99699229c6f938e6a8f6002f49eb4a3e9491f07052042d3592de90319b9a55f0-regular-push-sto.png)
